title: Fuck 9/11
author: Ken Klippenstein
content:

Twenty-five years later, 9/11 anniversaries have devolved into a grotesque
fundraising orgy for the security state.

The families commemorate their loved ones while the very security institutions
that failed to prevent the attack in the first place tell triumphant war
stories and warn that if we (the American people) let down our guard -- by
which they mean close our wallets to them -- it will happen again.

"The 9/11 attack took place without warning," Secretary of State Marco Rubio
writes to his employees today, per a memo leaked to me. After opening with
chest-beating ("We have hunted down the architects of the attack…"),
practically all he can say is: _don 't let your guard down_.

When it comes to the 9/11 anniversary, fundraising has become more and more
dominant. But it used to have a heart as well. In the days after the attacks,
Union Square in New York disappeared under candles and handwritten notes.
Flowers piled up outside firehouses that had lost entire crews. People waited
in line for hours to give blood, even though, as it turned out, there would be
almost no one to give it to.

The outpouring of sympathy was international, too. In Paris, _Le Monde_ ran a
front page declaring "Nous sommes tous Americains." At Buckingham Palace, the
band played the Star-Spangled Banner at the changing of the guard.

Now it's just a naked cash grab by the national security world, who
congratulate themselves for a job well done while angling for more money.

If this is all 9/11 remembrance is going to be, then I say: fuck 9/11.

Having no anniversary would be less offensive than what they've turned this
day into.

The whole thing reminds me of those money booths on game shows, where a
contestant stands inside a glass box while cash blows around them, grabbing at
as many bills as they can before time runs out.

Then there's the total lack of accountability from the security elite for what
was the most catastrophic intelligence failure since Pearl Harbor.

"Whether you like Dick Cheney or not, he was incredible on that day," Matthew
Waxman, a Bush National Security Council official at the time,
[said](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=90hEroSbC-8) at a discussion panel
about 9/11 at Columbia University this week.

Let's assume that's true. His job is to prevent attacks like these from
happening in the first place!

"I think there were some things that we got wrong, but many things that we
actually got quite right," Waxman added.

Notice something about all these panels, interviews and anniversary addresses:
The story always starts _after the_ first plane hit. Never before. Nobody
wants to talk about the August 6, 2001 President's Daily Brief titled "Bin
Ladin Determined To Strike in US." Or the FBI agent in Phoenix who warned
about extremists training at American flight schools. Or the CIA knowing two
of the future hijackers were in the country and not telling the FBI.

At that Columbia panel, Hillary Clinton recalled going to the Oval Office with
Chuck Schumer two days after the attacks.

"I looked at President Bush, and I thought, you know, my gosh, my heart went
out to him. I mean, just looking at his face, looking at his eyes, I thought,
you know, he is now at a totally different level of responsibility for this
country."

Our political elites have turned 9/11 into an episode of _The West Wing_ ,
starring themselves: the protagonists up on Mount Olympus, hitting their big
cinematic moment. The families seldom figure into these stories. The nation,
which has paid the greatest price in lost liberties, is not thanked or even
addressed much at all.

Then she got to the money. By her account, she told Bush the first bill his
team sent up had no money for New York. He asked what they needed. She said
$20 billion. Bush's answer: "You got it."

What happened next is the part she seems to relish.

"As I was getting up to leave the Oval Office, John Warner, one of my
absolutely favorite colleagues, a long-serving Republican senator who had
chaired the Senate Armed Services Committee forever, he touched me on the
shoulder, and he goes, 'Hillary, get him to say that in front of everybody
again.'"

Here's what didn't make it into her story: Bush's promise kicked off a fight
in Washington, because the White House's original $20 billion request was
supposed to cover the entire federal response. Congress settled it by doubling
the emergency package to $40 billion, with half set aside for recovery -- and
much of the rest flowing to the national security apparatus.

In other words, within days of the attacks, 9/11 was already a fundraising
event.

These days, 9/11 anniversaries have about as much to do with the nearly 3,000
people who died as Christmas has to do with Christ.

Consider an [anecdote](https://ptleader.com/articles/columns/allies-make-
united-states-stronger/) from retired Navy Capt. Brian Cullen, who had just
been posted to U.S. European Command in Stuttgart, Germany, when the planes
hit.

As U.S. bases across Europe went into lockdown, Germany rallied behind America
in a way that's hard to imagine today. Chancellor Gerhard Schroder pledged
"unlimited solidarity." Huge crowds filled the streets of Berlin. NATO invoked
Article 5, its mutual-defense clause, for the first time in its history.

But what stuck with Cullen was closer to home: German neighbors, kids
included, holding candlelight vigils outside the base gates -- the same gates
that usually drew anti-nuclear and anti-base protesters.

Then Washington pivoted to "you're either with us or against us," and the
goodwill evaporated. The candles disappeared. The base walled itself off from
the community around it. The alliance started to crack as the U.S. went it
alone.

"Our base became a reflection of our nation: security at any cost," Cullen
[writes](https://ptleader.com/articles/columns/allies-make-united-states-
stronger/).

That's the real legacy of 9/11. It was the beginning of the national security
state's soft coup over American politics, as my editor Bill Arkin laid out in
his profound [book](https://www.amazon.com/American-Coup-Government-
Destroying-Constitution-
ebook/dp/B00BAXFEZC/ref=sr_1_1?crid=2QE7CCYXHK85D&dib=eyJ2IjoiMSJ9.lPwePKFin5bN21JcEuCLHuFr4d7lWuDJPBkD-

_American Coup_.

We'll know that coup has ended when we see flowers again.
